Create an output specification

Source: R/recipe.R
omop_output.Rd

Defines how to shape the extracted data into a result table. Each output selects a subset of variables from the recipe, targets a population, and specifies a layout type (e.g. wide person-level, long event-level, or feature matrix). Outputs are passed to omop_recipe via its outputs argument and determine the server-side plan structure produced by recipe_to_plan.

Usage

omop_output(
  name = "output_1",
  type = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  population_id = "base",
  options = list(),
  result_symbol = NULL,
  rows = NULL,
  grain = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  format = NULL,
  sources = NULL,
  collapse = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Character; output table name (used as key in the recipe).

type

Character; output layout type. One of "wide", "long", "features", "survival", "intervals", "baseline", "temporal_covariates", or "person_period". A "long" output that spans multiple source tables always splits into one per-table output (named <name>_<table>); there is no single cross-table joined frame. The former "joined_long" label is rejected because it had no faithful executable mapping; use split "long" outputs. The "covariates_sparse" label (2.10.3, B-22) is the language-2 format = "sparse" over the output's variables as sources; it has no v1 rendering and runs on dsOMOP 2.10.3 servers.

variables

Character vector or NULL; variable names to include (NULL means all variables in the recipe).

population_id

Character; which population to use (default "base").

options

Named list; type-specific options (e.g. tar for survival outputs).

result_symbol

Character or NULL; R symbol name for the result on the server (auto-generated as D_<name> if NULL).

rows

(2.10.3) Alias of population_id (give one).

grain

(2.10.3) "episode" or "person"; default episode over an indexed population, person otherwise. Person grain over an indexed population needs collapse.

columns

(2.10.3) Alias of variables (give one).

format

(2.10.3) Language-2 format: "wide", "long", "survival", "intervals", "temporal_covariates", "person_period", "sparse", "membership", "dictionary" or "joined". type (the legacy presets) and format are alternatives; giving neither keeps the legacy type = "wide".

sources

(2.10.3) Event/era sources of a long output.

collapse

(2.10.3) "first_episode", "last_episode" or "any": person grain over an indexed population.

Value

An omop_output object.

Details

The baseline preset reports age as the banded legacy age_group (the server's default grid), while a wide output with omop_age() reports exact annual age; omop_age(bands = TRUE/FALSE, age_breaks =) chooses explicitly in every format, and recipe_explain() states the choice.

Survival outputs keep the legacy 730-day time-at-risk default when no tar/tars is given (print(), recipe_explain() and recipe_lint() state it); give tar = omop_window(1, NULL) for unbounded follow-up. A language-2 survival output needs an explicit censor list: only listed sources cap follow-up.

See also

omop_recipe, recipe_to_plan

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
recipe <- omop_recipe(
  variables = omop_variable(table = "condition_occurrence",
                            concept_id = 201820, format = "binary"),
  outputs = omop_output(name = "features_wide", type = "wide")
)
} # }
